items.title: 'If they put me in the freezer, I don't give a s***': Husic lashes Labor culture after push for Gaza debate fails
items.description: A push to recognise claims of genocide in Gaza failed to gain enough support for a debate on the floor of Labor's national conference, sparking criticism of the party's internal culture.

items.title: Houthis and Saudi Arabia trade fire amid Red Sea blockade
items.description: Houthi rebels have claimed a missile attack on Saudia Arabia's southern city of Jazan, after Riyadh struck military targets in Yemen following the Iran-backed group's Red Sea blockade.

items.title: Two people shot by police during altercation in Cairns
items.description: Police say a woman and a man have been shot in Cairns during an altercation with an armed suspect.

items.title: Drivers urged to play their part as five people die on WA roads in 24 hours
items.description: Five people have been killed in separate crashes in Western Australia in less than 24 hours, as the state's road toll continues to soar.

items.title: Indian education minister resigns after protests
items.description: Protesters have been calling for Dharmandra Pradhan's resignation amid ongoing exam paper leaks, which the education minister claims he "took responsibility" for.

items.title: Live: Dolphins to continue dominance in the pool as netball gets underway
items.description: Day two of the Commonwealth Games will see Australia start its netball gold medal defence against Tonga and the Dolphins swim team add more medals to the tally. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Cowboys and Broncos fight out another Queensland derby
items.description: The Broncos and Cowboys are at it again in the latest instalment of the NRL's great Queensland rivalry. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Tigers looking to challenge Dogs, Hawks and Swans dominate
items.description: Hawthorn records a 93-point win over Essendon at the MCG as Sydney puts GWS to the sword in the Battle of the Bridge. Follow live.

items.title: Iran's attacks on US bases in the Middle East mark 'end of an era'
items.description: Five months into a war Donald Trump said would last only weeks, the Iran conflict has so far cost the United States tens of billions of dollars and brought about "the end of an era" in American military strategy.

items.title: An addiction started at school landed Clay in a maximum-security prison
items.description: Clay first tried drugs during lunchtime at school. What followed was a decade of addiction and run-ins with police. Now he hopes sharing his story will help others.

items.title: How Black teenager's death has rocked the US Deep South into racial division
items.description: Black teen Nolan Wells went to a party with white friends and didn't come home alive. His death is now shrouded in rampant speculation and an air of racial division.

items.title: Japan's royal crisis sparks debate about women on the throne
items.description: There are only three people in line to inherit Japan's Chrysanthemum Throne, and one of them is 90 years old. All three of them are men.

items.title: Trump mixes jokes with barbs at press freedom dinner
items.description: US President Donald Trump has poked fun at the press during a redo of the White House Correspondents' Association dinner after a shooting forced the suspension of the original event in April.

items.title: Federal government says fuel supply 'solid and secure' as prices climb again
items.description: The government is reassuring motorists about Australia's fuel supply as petrol prices rise amid renewed clashes in the five-month old war in the Middle East.

items.title: Dog trainer says ABC's Muster Dogs is driving demand for working dogs
items.description: Gary White travels the world teaching people how to get the most out of their working dog. Lately, he's seen strong demand for working dogs, in part thanks to ABC's hit series Muster Dogs.

items.title: Emelia Jackson's French yoghurt cake is the epitome of easy
items.description: A simple, comforting and kid-friendly cake using yoghurt.

items.title: Farmers kept planting as the war raged and now they are paying for it
items.description: North Queensland farmers urge consumers to eat more vegetables as rising costs and low demand create a "perfect storm".

items.title: Here's what you need to know about Woodside's Federal Court case
items.description: Four days in, the Federal Court has scrutinised the decision to extend Australia's biggest gas project another 40 years, amid fears for Indigenous heritage and climate impacts.

items.title: H5 bird flu confirmed in wild seabird found at Moreton Island
items.description: The CSIRO has officially confirmed a dead petrel found at Moreton Island was positive for H5 bird flu.

items.title: Two new bird flu cases suspected in SA, including first on a metro beach
items.description: Two additional suspected cases of H5 bird flu have been detected in South Australia.

items.title: Liberty Bell Bay may have been insolvent for more than a year before closing
items.description: Administrators say the manganese smelter was insolvent before it was given a $20 million loan by the Tasmanian government.

items.title: 'If you get cancer, you will go bankrupt': Anna Funder on life in the US
items.description: The award-winning author, who burst onto the literary scene with her debut, Stasiland, in 2003, discusses writing, AI and the rise of fascism.

items.title: Thousands flock to Victorian canola farm chasing social media snaps
items.description: Tourists looking to get a picture of canola fields are often told to steer clear, but one central Victorian farm is welcoming them with open arms and has turned the attraction into a popular agritourism event.

items.title: Man dead, police officer shot in domestic violence callout
items.description: Police were responding to a domestic violence incident west of Maryborough when a man allegedly opened fire on Friday night.

items.title: Bali bans two Dutch men alleged to have hosted discriminatory run club
items.description: Bali's Immigration department bans two Dutch expats from Indonesia for organising a run club event "fraught with discrimination against local residents".
